issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry strips all OTLP LoggingHandlers from the root logger, mutating global state it does not own.
issues.detail: The function removes every LoggingHandler on the root logger, not just the one this module installed. In embedding or multi-job hosts, this rips out handlers attached by user code. Hold a reference to the handler created in _setup_cloud_tracer and detach only that one.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer locates the OTLP handler by scanning root handlers instead of using a stored reference.
issues.detail: The replay code imports LoggingHandler and picks the first isinstance match on the root logger. If any other OTLP LoggingHandler exists, replay goes to the wrong one and crash logs are lost. _setup_cloud_tracer knows exactly which handler it installed; store and pass that reference rather than guessing.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is an unbounded list with no size cap.
issues.detail: If a job hangs before init_recording or logs heavily before OTLP wires up, the buffer grows without limit and can OOM the worker. Use a bounded deque(maxlen=N) or ring-buffer with drop-oldest semantics, and state the invariant explicitly. A crash-log feature that OOMs is worse than the bug it fixes.

issues.description: Unrelated worker.py race fix and makefile test-infra changes are bundled into a crash-log patch.
issues.detail: The PR mixes three concerns: log buffering, a worker.py pending-assignment race fix, and removal of pytest-xdist plus test_plugin_google_stt.py. Split into separate commits so bisect, revert, and review work cleanly. At minimum add a one-line comment on the worker.py reorder explaining why it must precede _queue_msg.

issues.description: JobContext leaks telemetry implementation details through scattered lifecycle methods and init_recording overload.
issues.detail: _start_log_buffering, _stop_log_buffering, _flush_early_log_buffer, and the _on_cleanup branch calling init_recording with synthetic options all manage one handler across two modules. Encapsulate as a LogBuffer object owning attach/detach/replay in the telemetry module, and give crash-log flushing its own narrow entry point instead of reusing init_recording.

issues.description: Bare except Exception in _on_cleanup around init_recording can leak half-initialized telemetry state.
issues.detail: The broad catch logs and then only runs _stop_log_buffering on the failure path. If init_recording raises after partially wiring OTLP, shutdown inherits inconsistent state. Narrow the exception class or ensure _stop_log_buffering runs unconditionally in a finally block before propagating unexpected errors.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the crash-log upload approach (buffer early, replay through OTLP, flush on cleanup) is the right shape but the execution leaks abstraction boundaries. Two P0 problems: _shutdown_telemetry mutates root logger handlers it does not own, and _flush_early_log_buffer locates the OTLP handler by isinstance scan rather than holding the reference _setup_cloud_tracer created. The buffer is also unbounded, risking OOM on stalled startup. Additionally, unrelated worker.py race fix and makefile test-infra changes should be split out. Fix handler scoping, cap the buffer, encapsulate the buffering lifecycle, and separate the unrelated changes.
